summary: Iteration 6 tested 3 new features — (A) Trip archive/unarchive/delete (organizer-only, with cascade), (B) Chat unread badges + notification dedup, (C) Recap share link (/api/recap/{token}/share HTML page + /og.png card). Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_iter6_features.py with 10 pytest tests — all 10 PASS (61s). Covers: archive/unarchive by organizer returns {ok:true,archived:true/false}; non-organizer POST /archive & /unarchive → 403; list_trips shows archived flag; non-organizer DELETE → 403; organizer DELETE cascades (expenses, settlements, trip_messages, chat_reads collections empty for trip_id; memories soft-deleted; recap token → 404; GET /api/trips/{id} → 404); GET /api/trips/{id}/messages/unread returns count of msgs from OTHERS since last read (own posts don't count); POST /api/trips/{id}/messages/read clears count; GET /api/trips includes unread_chat per trip; chat_message notification dedup — sender posts 2 msgs, recipient has exactly 1 unread chat_message notif ("Name: text" format); after recipient marks read + sender posts again, a NEW notif is created; GET /api/recap/{token}/share is PUBLIC HTML 200 containing trip name, og:image → /api/recap/{token}/og.png, meta-refresh + location.replace to /recap/{token}; GET /api/recap/{token}/og.png returns image/png 1200x630 with PNG magic bytes; invalid token → 404 on both endpoints. Frontend Playwright (as aarav organizer + meera member cross-user): trip-menu-btn visible for organizer, dropdown has trip-archive-btn + trip-delete-btn ✓; clicking archive shows trip-archived-badge + reopening menu label becomes 'Unarchive trip' ✓; on /trips main grid the archived trip disappears, toggle-archived-btn shows 'Archived trips (N)', clicking reveals archived-trips-section with the card ✓; trip-delete-btn opens delete-trip-dialog, confirm-delete-trip-btn deletes + redirects to /trips + card gone from list ✓; cross-user chat: aarav posts 2 msgs → meera's /trips shows trip-chat-unread-badge '2 new' ✓, opening trip detail shows chat-unread-badge '2' on Chat tab ✓, meera's notifications-bell shows exactly one 'New messages in TEST_UI_Chat_... — Aarav Sharma: msg 1' notification ✓, clicking trip-tab-chat clears the badge (count=0) ✓; meera (non-organizer) does NOT see trip-menu-btn ✓; Memories tab copy-recap-link-btn copies URL {origin}/api/recap/{token}/share to clipboard ✓, GET on that URL returns 200 HTML containing og:title, og:image → /api/recap/{token}/og.png, and refresh/redirect to /recap/{token} ✓; visiting the /api/recap/.../share URL redirects to /recap/{token} slideshow which renders 'THE STORY OF <trip name>' + Paris dates ✓. Regression: chat send/receive works, trips create/list/delete work, notifications bell still lists prior notification types (Added to trip, Trip deleted).

issues: Navigating to /trips/{deleted_id} shows an indefinite 'Loading trip…' state with no 404/error UI. Observed while trying to open the deleted iter5 EUR trip 6a6b277497fc9f4f0c14ea00. Consider handling 404 from GET /api/trips/{id} with a 'Trip not found' state + back-to-trips CTA.

action_items: LOW: On TripDetail, when GET /api/trips/{id} returns 404 (trip deleted or invalid), replace the perpetual 'Loading trip…' spinner with a 'Trip not found' empty-state + link back to /trips.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/routers_trips.py delete_trip: cascade deletes are not wrapped in a transaction and are non-atomic — if the process is killed between deleting expenses and deleting the trip doc, orphan data may persist. For MongoDB replica set, consider a client.start_session() + with_transaction wrapper, or at minimum delete the trip doc LAST so a mid-flight failure leaves the trip visible with best-effort re-run possible.

backend/routers_trips.py delete_trip does not delete uploaded memory FILES from disk/storage (memories are only soft-deleted via is_deleted=True). Over time this will leak storage for permanently-deleted trips. Add a background storage sweeper or hard-delete files when parent trip is deleted.

backend/routers_trips.py chat_message notification dedup queries {read:False} but does NOT restrict by created_at, meaning a very old unread notif from months ago will suppress new chat notifs. Consider also matching data.trip_id + a freshness window, or refresh the existing notif's message/created_at when a new msg arrives so users see the latest sender/text.

backend/routers_memories.py recap_share_page builds `origin = f'https://{host}'` from x-forwarded-host / host — behind proxies without x-forwarded-proto this may still be correct but is fragile. Prefer request.url.scheme (or trust proxy header explicitly).
frontend/src/pages/TripDetail.jsx: no error/404 state for the initial trip fetch — page stays on 'Loading trip…' when trip is missing (see design_issues).

success_rate.frontend: 100% (menu, archive+badge+unarchive label, archived section on list, delete flow, cross-user chat unread badges on list + tab, notif bell 'New messages in', badge clears on chat tab open, non-organizer no menu, share link copy + HTML meta + redirect to slideshow)

seed_data_creation: Test file creates ~7 short-lived TEST_-prefixed trips and cleans them up via new DELETE endpoint after each test. Frontend playwright cleaned all TEST_UI_ trips at end. No lingering test data expected. The pre-existing iter5 EUR fixture trip 6a6b277497fc9f4f0c14ea00 is GONE (404) — appears to have been cleaned up between iterations; recap flow was retested on a freshly created trip.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All iter6 features PASS. Backend tests in /app/backend/tests/test_iter6_features.py use the requests retry wrapper (documented since iter1) and self-clean TEST_ trips. DELETE /api/trips/{id} is now available and used for cleanup. The prior iter5 EUR trip 6a6b277497fc9f4f0c14ea00 no longer exists. When retesting the recap share flow, create a fresh trip and click copy-recap-link-btn on Memories tab; no memory upload is required for the button to appear.
rca_of_the_issue: No functional defects found in the 3 new features. Only observation: TripDetail lacks a 404/not-found UI when the trip id is invalid or deleted — noted as LOW design issue.
